title: Kapiʻolani
summary: Kapiʻolani was a high-ranking Hawaiian woman, born in Hilo around 1781, who with her husband Naihe welcomed missionaries in the early 1820s. In late 1824 she travelled to Kīlauea to challenge belief in the goddess Pele, ignoring warnings from Pele's priestess. She died on 5 May 1841.

uncertainty.note: Birth is given only as "around 1781"; death date is given as 5 May 1841.

as_recorded.value: Born in Hilo, on the island of Hawaii, around 1781

where.modern_name: Halemaʻumaʻu crater, Kīlauea, Hawaiʻi Island (pin on the site of her 1824 defiance of Pele; she was born in Hilo)
where.historical_name: Kīlauea volcano, island of Hawaiʻi, in the Hawaiian kingdom

importance.justification: A leading chiefess whose 1824 defiance of Pele became a landmark in the spread of Christianity in Hawaiʻi.

sources.title: Hawaiian Legends of Volcanoes, XX. Kapiolani and Pele

reviewer_note: Sources differ on the month of the 1824 visit: Encyclopedia.com says the fall of 1824 and the older Westervelt text says December 1824. Both call the act a defiance of Pele rather than giving a fixed hour or exact spot. The pin marks the site of the act, not her birthplace or residence.
